product: ECHO keeps a moving inspection application responsive by selecting a suitable network and processing server, preparing the target, and transferring session progress before switching.

controller_modes.label: TCP reconnect baseline
controller_modes.summary: Stays on one TCP connection until it breaks, then dials again and rebuilds the session from nothing.

controller_modes.label: QUIC with fixed server
controller_modes.summary: The QUIC connection follows the robot across networks, but processing never leaves the first server.

controller_modes.label: Measurement-driven migration
controller_modes.summary: ECHO moves the session using smoothed current measurements (no forecast). Demonstration default.

controller_modes.label: Predictive migration
controller_modes.summary: ECHO moves the session using a 2-second trend forecast. Experimental option.

application_profiles.label: Interactive inspection
application_profiles.description: Live camera frames. Upcoming frames cannot be fetched early, and a late result loses its value.

application_profiles.label: Buffered playback
application_profiles.description: Prerecorded content. Upcoming segments can be fetched ahead, so a short delivery interruption can be hidden.

status.detail: Real aioquic connections on loopback. The connection keeps its identity when the robot's network changes.
Real TCP sockets; reconnects and rebuilds the session after a break.
Delay, jitter, loss and bandwidth applied by userspace relays (the tc/netem idea), driven by the scenario.
Four independent server services. Processing is a controlled delay that responds to load and cold starts; no detector model runs.
Session id, state version and last completed request are transferred and checked before and after the switch. The tracking content is synthetic, so no tracking accuracy is claimed.

status.item: Four controller modes in one engine
status.detail: TCP reconnect, QUIC fixed server, measurement-driven and predictive migration; same scenario, workload and seed.
Deterministic test event (scenario C), shown as a test event.
Chosen explicitly. Automatic recognition of applications from encrypted traffic is not claimed; a traffic-shape classifier only advises and answers 'unknown' when unsure.
A controlled segment workload with a measured buffer and stall counter. Not a real video player, and not YouTube.
A link profile with satellite-like delay. No satellite terminal is controlled.
Generated deterministically from the decision's own numbers. No language model is used.
